chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said:

He (عليه السلام) came out to me, so I looked at his head and his feet so that I might describe his stature to our companions in Miṣr. While I was in that state, he sat and said: O ʿAlī, indeed Allah argued regarding the Imamate with the like of what He argued regarding Prophethood, and so He said:
"And We gave him wisdom while yet a child."

He said: "And when he reached his maturity," and "reaches forty years"; thus it is possible that wisdom be given while one is a child, and it is possible that it be given to him while he is a son of forty years.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً: forty years of age, indicating mature adulthood
key_terms.النُّبُوَّةِ: Prophethood as a parallel divine office used here for comparison
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةِ: the divinely appointed leadership of the Imam
key_terms.الْحُكْمَ: divine wisdom or authority granted by Allah
key_terms.صَبِيًّا: in a state of childhood or young age

ai.seo_question: Can an Imam be appointed by Allah while still a child?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the argument that Imamate, like Prophethood, is established by Allah and is not restricted to old age or conventional expectations. By citing Quranic examples of divine wisdom being granted in childhood and at forty years, the Imam عليه السلام shows that Allah appoints His proof whenever He wills.
